headline: High-risk workflow pair: n8n can write and execute server-side actions while Plane ingests files and broad network content, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute command/code nodes, so attacker-controlled content from Plane files or issue text could be treated as workflow input. Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, giving a plausible bridge, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest Plane issue text, uploaded files, or hyperlinks as prompts or instructions
IF a Plane attachment contains untrusted instructions that a downstream n8n node parses as trusted content
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any n8n AI Agent node consumes Plane content
Strip instructions from uploaded files before passing them into n8n
Use allowlisted fields only, not full issue bodies or attachments
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every Plane-to-n8n payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and can access the server filesystem plus broad egress; Plane stores issues, tasks, files, images, and notes. If the pair shares a workspace or workflow, sensitive Plane data can flow into n8n outputs or external integrations. The exact shared storage is not documented, so I choose medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Plane files or notes are passed into an n8n workflow that calls external integrations
IF both systems are configured to access the same server filesystem or shared upload directory
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to redacted metadata only
Separate Plane uploads from n8n-readable directories
Disable unnecessary outbound integrations in n8n
Review credential scopes for every connected node
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before any external API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad network egress, while Plane has broad network egress and file uploads. They can contend over shared mutable resources if deployed against the same workspace or connected systems. Because Plane lacks filesystem write, this is not the high-severity same-dir write conflict, but overlap is still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared upload directory or connected backend
IF n8n workflows write artifacts that Plane later reads or indexes
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each system
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use per-workflow locks in the orchestrator
Check for duplicate updates before saving
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate tools and execute server-side actions, so if Plane outputs issues, tasks, or notes that n8n treats as authoritative, errors can cascade into irreversible external actions. Plane’s content types are broad and n8n’s automation surface is powerful, making the default pathway dangerous unless explicit verification is added.
conditions: IF n8n uses Plane issue text or task fields as direct triggers for emails, deployments, or shell commands
IF no verification step checks Plane-derived facts before n8n acts
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before action nodes
Require schema validation on Plane-derived inputs
Log and diff every automated action against source records
Limit n8n to read-only summarization for Plane data
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback hooks

E_compliance.rationale: Plane handles issues, tasks, files, images, and notes, while n8n can move whatever the workflow processes through broad egress and external integrations. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if regulated data from Plane is routed through n8n-connected services. No specific residency or certification data is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from Plane is sent through n8n integrations hosted in another jurisdiction
IF retention settings differ between Plane storage and downstream n8n-connected services
mitigations: Classify Plane data before routing it into n8n
Block regulated fields from outbound integrations
Document retention for each connected node
Confirm hosting region for every external service
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
